title: On the desk
intro: A few things in motion, a few ideas for later. Nothing here is a deadline ~

items.title: Desktop performance and display pass
items.detail: Compact through 4K layouts and 200% browser zoom checked in Firefox, Edge and Chrome. Timeline can reopen and filter without rebuilding its data. These checks do not certify frame pacing on physical displays or screen-reader behavior.

items.title: Align minimized windows with the content
items.detail: The desktop restore controls and System Tips align with the workspace's right rail, above the footer. Existing restore behavior is unchanged.

items.title: Dashboard: digital chrome and system tips
items.detail: Explore a hologram-style time and date readout, with distinct cipher and glitch resolves for the Dashboard and footer. Replace the public System Tips button with a bell at the same location as the local publish bell; the public bell keeps tips available even if the welcome prompt is missed. Local publishing stays unchanged.

items.title: Setup overhaul
items.detail: The last section design pass, after Logs. Revisit the device bay while keeping Systems, Tools, Peripherals and Notes, along with their in-place editing. Design to be discussed.

items.title: Archive Relay
items.detail: Discuss after Setup editing. A writing and research companion above Connections: chat, keep a note alongside it, minimize and return. Account support, privacy and public access need checking first; everyone would use their own connection. Simple two-window tiling could follow later. Not in development yet.

items.title: Power-on, one beat and the Field Desk
items.detail: Gestalt powers on in about three seconds and reports what it actually read, including your last session when local memory is on. The power-on line becomes the header rule, and Memory State logs the boot. Records open and close on one clean beat. Logs sits on a lamp-lit Field Desk, and every section shares the Dashboard's plates.

items.title: Workbench, drive and lit screens
items.detail: Every section fills the same frame. Projects keeps every project on a spine and spreads the selected one across the bay, with its milestones, newest note and a lit screen. Games loads the current game into a drive beside the shelves. At Night the plates are solid and the screens glow with their own pictures; Weather draws the next twelve hours.

items.title: Field Papers
items.detail: Logs lie on the desk as a short stack of papers. Open the front sheet to read it, or bring another forward by its edge. Handheld shows one sheet with readable spines. The newest three stay on the desk; older logs still file into the Field Archive after seven days.

items.title: The Dashboard lives behind Terminal
items.detail: Open Terminal with T and the surrounding signals keep moving. Memory State writes the action while the Terminal is still open. The workspace stays non-interactive behind it, and Reduced Motion still applies.

items.title: Dashboard plates and live readouts
items.detail: All six plates share a raised finish and a small mouse response that stays inside the grid. Projects gets a short scanner, Latest Log keeps its excerpt steady, Current Game has a recessed LCD, and Memory State's code glows at the characters. Touch and Reduced Motion skip the hover movement.

items.title: A new backdrop for Day
items.detail: A misty hydroelectric spillway gives Day its own scenery. Night keeps the original image, and startup only preloads the backdrop for the selected appearance.

items.title: Clearer tape labels and fresher starts
items.detail: Handheld VHS titles wrap without clipped letters, even in a short viewport. Pages revalidates the shell on return visits without discarding cached media.

items.title: Steadier cipher and lighter Setup
items.detail: The signal has its own character spacing and reveals the readable line in steps. Setup tiles no longer parse terminal specs. Handheld Games search keeps its tap target with a bare icon and a slim input.

items.title: Pocket libraries and a sharper cipher
items.detail: Games gets full-height upright tapes with handwritten labels and search beside Back. Projects uses tall cards with vertical titles. Swipe across records or vertically to change groups. Gestalt's cipher now cycles glyphs and locks text into place, with no movement for Reduced Motion.

items.title: Upright tapes and a vertical Process Reader
items.detail: Two upright VHS tapes fit side by side in the handheld Media Cabinet, and search stays within the header. Projects scroll vertically within each group. Swipe sideways or tap either group button to switch, with no project arrows on handheld. Desktop keeps its original controls.

items.title: Pocket Index: tapes and touch controls
items.detail: The handheld Media Cabinet uses wide VHS cassettes with readable labels and twin reels. The next tape peeks in from the edge. The Process Reader drops its dropdown: tap a group, swipe the plate or use the arrows, and tap the plate to open the record. Desktop floppies and project rotation stay in place.

items.title: Pocket Index: a shelf and a workplate
items.detail: Games uses one swipeable shelf with Session Logs and Past Logs switches. Each shelf remembers its position, and search checks both. Projects uses a grouped picker and a stationary plate with progress and its most relevant milestone. Desktop keeps its original controls and rotation.

items.title: Write in place across the archive
items.detail: The local gear opens the exact Project or Game note for editing. Single-note Logs and Setup Notes go straight to a framed writer with formatting and media tools. Multi-note records keep their files. Save Record writes locally; the bell still reviews and publishes separately. Pages stays read-only.

items.title: Focus without the outer box
items.detail: Keyboard navigation and Escape keep a clear focus cue inside the control instead of drawing a square that can clip against a window or shelf.

items.title: One file directory for Games and Projects
items.detail: Open an entry and browse its notes as files, up to six across on desktop and two on handheld, without paging. Search stays in the tab bar, and closing a note returns you to the same file. Project windows use the project name and only show Technical Stack or Samples when there is something to see.

items.title: Logs open straight to the writing
items.detail: Logs skip the overview and open directly to the full note. References, dates, status and exact note links stay intact. Attachments have their own tab only when present. The editor is unchanged.

items.title: Projects and Games: a different way to browse
items.detail: Projects gets its own Process Reader. Active Projects and Other Projects use cycling workplates instead of long lists, with real statuses, progress and milestone traces. Active plates turn mechanically; the quieter Other Projects plates register with a brief glitch. Hover brings up a slow glow, and pressing the plate opens its record.

items.title: Games: the Media Cabinet
items.detail: Session Logs and Past Logs now sit on separate shelves of Gestalt floppy disks. Drag the shelves, scroll Past Logs with the wheel, or search from the section header. Hover lifts a disk and turns its hub; pressing it opens the existing entry. Inside, Overview, Notes and Recommendation share a title bar and artwork, and notes open as individual files.

items.title: Full Welcome and the desktop reading flow
items.detail: Full Welcome runs through 24 console lines and the operator screen before each dashboard module comes online with its own cue. Quick Start and handheld boot keep their existing behavior. Dashboard notes can open in a focused reader, and minimized windows and System Tips sit on the workspace rail.

items.title: Setup editing in place
items.detail: Edit systems, shortcut icons and links, peripheral photos and setup notes in their existing windows. Pocket Index opens single-note logs directly, and the Timeline reuses its results. Studio remains a fallback.

items.title: Pocket Index: easier reading and navigation
items.detail: Directory icons line up with section names. Switch between parts of an entry from the header, or search above the list when the entry has multiple notes.

items.title: Handheld scrolling and record references
items.detail: Entries are ready to scroll as the opening sequence finishes. Record badges no longer repeat the sort priority, and shared links still lead to the same entries and notes.

items.title: A consistent entry opening
items.detail: Handheld now has the full ACCESSING sequence, including the frame and sweep. Back stays available while the entry builds. Closing returns you to the same search result or dispatch.

items.title: Pocket Index: dispatches and a way home
items.detail: Tap GESTALT to return to the index. Recent Dispatches open straight to the note. Share controls stay out of the prose, and the short ACCESSING sequence can play on the first entry, on every entry, or not at all.

items.title: Search directly for a note
items.detail: The Command Palette can find individual notes by title and open them on the right page. Each result shows its parent entry and the note date when available. One-letter searches match the start of titles, and handheld Back returns to the search.

items.title: Link directly to a record or note
items.detail: Copy a record link from its window or a note link from the expanded note. Links open the right reading page, even for older notes and archived records. Back returns to the current browsing section.

items.title: Aligned reading panes
items.detail: Projects, Games and Logs share one pane height in wide Terminal mode. The Reading Desk stays full height even with only a few logs, and longer lists scroll without moving the bottom edge.

items.title: Find the right note
items.detail: Recent Activity lists individual notes, even when two belong to the same entry. Long entries show five notes per page, with search across the whole record. A direct link opens the right note, and Escape closes it without changing the list first. Current Game shows an authored summary with playtime and last played, and System Tips has its own info icon.

items.title: Pocket browsing and a quieter Memory State
items.detail: Handheld Games and Projects show four records per group at a time and keep your page when you close an entry. Memory State drops the inner filename and keeps a faint frame around its code lines.

items.title: Handheld edge fit
items.detail: The Pocket Index fills the phone viewport while keeping controls clear of the notch and home indicator. Supported mobile browser bars follow Day and Night mode.

items.title: Pocket Index
items.detail: The handheld archive opens into a numbered directory instead of a floating dock. Search and Settings are up front, and Back returns you from a full-screen record to where you were. The short field boot has a variable progress bar, a scan-line handoff and a reduced-motion skip.

items.title: Lighter first load
items.detail: The same Day and Night backdrop now downloads as a full-resolution WebP, about 92% smaller. The original artwork and boot sequence stay intact.

items.title: Room to read
items.detail: Dashboard cards scroll intact on compact desktops and at high zoom. Day headers reveal more of the artwork, older game covers stay visible across entry tabs, and Archive folders use the same scrollbars as the rest of Gestalt.

items.title: Keep the archive in place
items.detail: Switch sections and open Timeline, Roadmap or a month folder without rebuilding the page. Folder browsing preserves the index and its scroll. Escape closes reading entries after nested controls, without closing an inline editor.

items.title: Less repeated workspace work
items.detail: Stable readouts reuse their results, closed search stays idle and Memory State avoids unchanged layout measurements. Settings keeps the workspace in place, and the palette stays usable above entries. The wider browser and display review continues.

items.title: Month-by-month folders
items.detail: Recent field notes stay loose while complete older months settle into MM/YYYY folders when the archive grows past 24 notes. Keep at least 12 recent files and their complete months within reach. Same file-manager windows, original writing order and content files.

items.title: Quieter ambient rhythms
items.detail: Project traces, log scans, cover glow, NEW chips, weather and seasonal details each have their own rhythm and quiet rests. Same artwork and layout, with text kept still. Hidden and covered effects pause reliably in either Memory State mode.

items.title: Memory State code surface
items.detail: Short code-like sequences respond to actions, with quiet idle passages between them. The one-way stream drops hidden lines while its numbering continues. Legacy Visual stays on the left in Settings; Code Surface sits on the right.

items.title: Timeline arrival
items.detail: A brief register-line and reading-area arrival in both readers. Filtering keeps its place without replaying the entrance, and keyboard focus stays inside the timeline.

items.title: Window control harmony
items.detail: Entry and notebook edit gears sit beside the other window controls, matching Setup. The existing sizes, editing actions and public read-only boundaries stay intact.

items.title: Quieter transition work
items.detail: Opening and closing entries retain the Pages workspace instead of rebuilding it. Fewer overlapping masks and fades, paused hidden effects and safer close/minimize cleanup reduce unnecessary work. Remaining browser differences stay on the desk.

items.title: Bounded notebook retrieval
items.detail: A stalled first request now reaches a retry state instead of waiting indefinitely. Late expired requests cannot overwrite newer notebook data.

items.title: Notebook editing in place
items.detail: A local gear opens editing on the page: change wording, add work and mark it complete. Drafts survive closing the window; saves stay local until published through the bell.

items.title: Dated notebook history
items.detail: Choose completed work, enter a release version and date, then save it into Filed. Older history stays intact and publishing remains a separate action.

items.title: Roomier windows and matching controls
items.detail: Normal entries are wider without changing height or mobile layout. Notebook and entry gears match the close controls, and completed notebook titles have a clearer strike-through in both themes.

items.title: Quote-safe recommendation saves
items.detail: Repeated saves retain quoted recommendation text without accumulating escape characters. The local reader and exported archive agree.

items.title: Desktop proportions and quieter background work
items.detail: Scaled reading labels and section manifests, consistent Archive footer spacing, shared reduced-motion-aware Memory State input, paused covered/offscreen effects and keyboard boundaries for record windows.

items.title: Day, Night and window depth
items.detail: A mineral-gray Day appearance alongside Night and local-clock Auto. Clearer labels, continuous window frames, tactile controls and slimmer entry bars, with permission-aware remembered preferences.

items.title: Startup and notebook settling
items.detail: Boot progress and brief signal interruptions vary between visits without extending startup. The notebook opens with lighter registration details; clicking its header or the Connections header no longer restarts the opening.

items.title: Independent publishing
items.detail: Saved notes publish against the committed site while unfinished visual work stays local. Interrupted publication can recover without sweeping unrelated code into a content update.

items.title: Record closing and winter details
items.detail: Closing dissolves the content before the frame contracts; minimizing keeps its own restore gesture. December and January join the calendar decorations, with seasonal details remaining optional.

items.title: Terminal and window gestures
items.detail: T opens a directory with real section dates and a compact restore icon. Search and Terminal construct their frames before the contents resolve; minimizing contracts toward the restore control without losing reading state. The greeting keeps up with local time and returning tabs.

items.title: Artwork and shortcuts
items.detail: Independent title-background framing for Projects and Games. Press S for a separate web-search bar that opens results in a new tab; Connections holds the public X and Reddit links behind its own signal-acquisition sequence.

items.title: Editing comforts
items.detail: Optional note-heading titles, styled native selectors and clear local save states. Progress labels keep focus while typing; unfinished recommendation and hardware text stays in a local draft when the editor closes. Saving and publishing remain separate.

items.title: System Notices
items.detail: First-visit shortcuts open a quiet reference tray beside minimized windows, then fade away when left alone. Remembered visits respect local-memory permission.

items.title: Settings and startup
items.detail: A square profile welcome and composed workspace arrival. A dedicated palette button controls entry animation, full or quick startup, seasonal details and Terminal or Legacy navigation. Remembered choices respect local-memory permission.

items.title: Section reading space
items.detail: Written project updates, game sessions and a field-note reading desk beside the existing lists.

items.title: A clearer timeline
items.detail: Recent signals grouped by date, with source selection and a more readable trail.

items.title: Editing in place
items.detail: Create, format and edit field notes, games and projects in their own windows. Saves stay local; the publishing bell reviews saved changes and publishes the batch separately from drafts.

items.title: Steam and artwork
items.detail: Automatic Current Game with playtime and achievements when available; adjustable game headers without changing original images.

items.title: Session and Past Logs
items.detail: Keep games to return to separate from completed or retired play logs.

items.title: Full-size media
items.detail: Open samples and screenshots outside the record window.

items.title: Field Archive
items.detail: A file-manager home for older notes, with original writing order preserved.

items.title: Logs keep their place
items.detail: Editing a field note no longer moves it up the archive. Empty summaries can use the note itself, and Studio adds its first block-formatting tools.

items.title: Safer saves and publish recovery
items.detail: Studio distinguishes a saved record from an export or publish failure. The archive can refresh its generated index without making you write the note again.

items.title: ACCESSING
items.detail: Opening a record gets an archive handshake: its frame draws in, a signal passes through it, and the contents come into view.

items.title: The first Field Archive
items.detail: Older logs get a home of their own, with folders to browse them. Studio gets a single place to review saved changes before publishing.

items.title: A launcher for Gestalt
items.detail: A Windows launcher opens the local archive without starting it by hand from a terminal. Editing controls are visible in the local reader, separate from the public archive.

items.title: From the archive to the editor
items.detail: Open an entry in the local archive and jump straight into editing that record, instead of finding it again in Studio.

items.title: Lighter media, original files kept
items.detail: Studio can create smaller display copies for notes. Readers still open the full image on demand. Studio styles are split away from the public reader.

items.title: Media survives an update
items.detail: Covers, screenshots and icons can stay in the browser cache across deployments, instead of downloading again with every archive update.

items.title: The Setup device bay
items.detail: Tools, peripherals, systems and notes get their own ways of opening. Apps can be shortcuts, photos can be viewed at full size, and system records keep their terminal.

items.title: Recent Activity becomes a ledger
items.detail: The desktop dashboard gets room to show both newer and older dispatches without crowding the entry titles.

items.title: Local memory is a choice
items.detail: The archive asks before remembering browser preferences. It still works when you choose to keep things to the current visit.

items.title: An atmosphere of its own
items.detail: The archive gains more of its own visual character through registration marks, layered surfaces and quieter details instead of making every panel look alike.

items.title: A terminal for Setup
items.detail: System records move out of the ordinary entry layout and into a terminal-style space for hardware and machine notes.

items.title: One tap to change sections
items.detail: An early handheld redesign puts the main sections on a bottom dock and moves the rest of the navigation into an on-demand menu.

items.title: The first handheld layout
items.detail: Small screens get their own navigation and way into records, the first step away from squeezing the desktop archive onto a phone.

items.title: The archive speaks in cipher
items.detail: Navigation gains its own glyphs, giving the sidebar a little mystery while keeping the original section names.

items.title: A chronology for the archive
items.detail: The first Timeline brings activity from different parts of Gestalt together in date order.

items.title: The Command Palette
items.detail: Search records and jump around the archive from one keyboard-friendly surface.

items.title: Publishing from Studio
items.detail: Studio begins publishing archive updates without a separate terminal command. Later versions separate local saves from the decision to publish.

items.title: An archive built for Pages
items.detail: The static archive is prepared for GitHub Pages, giving readers a way in without running the local app.

items.title: Studio starts to feel like the archive
items.detail: A reworked local editor brings record editing and artwork handling closer to the reading interface.

items.title: The first Steam sync
items.detail: The Persona 5 Royal record gets Steam stats alongside the hand-written play log.

items.title: A stack of session notes
items.detail: Game logs can hold individual notes so a new session adds to the record instead of rewriting the previous one.

items.title: Persona 5 Royal opens the play logs
items.detail: The first game record brings session writing and game artwork into the archive.

items.title: Memory State wakes up
items.detail: The first animated Memory State gives the dashboard a pulse of its own.

items.title: First Signal
items.detail: The earliest working Gestalt in Git: an archive in the shape of a little desktop, with its first field note and room for projects, play logs and setup records.
